name: Tagbreeze – Server-Side Tracking & Conversions API for WooCommerce
author: webotic

sections.description:
Tagbreeze is server-side tracking for WordPress and WooCommerce. It sends every purchase, lead and sign-up to the Meta (Facebook) Conversions API, the TikTok Events API, Google Analytics 4 and Google Ads, from the browser and from a server, with one event ID so each conversion is counted once.

Ad blockers, Safari’s cookie limits and buyers who close the tab before the thank-you page hide part of your sales from Meta, Google and TikTok. Their algorithms then optimise on half the picture. Tagbreeze sends each conversion by a second road, from its servers, without Google Tag Manager, without a tagging server to run, and without a developer.

This plugin connects your site to your Tagbreeze account (14-day free trial, no card).

Not sure what your site sends today? The free tracking check lists its Meta, Google and TikTok pixels, the duplicates and the consent tool in about ten seconds, with no sign-up.

Meta Conversions API (CAPI) and Facebook pixel

  • Purchases, leads, add to cart, checkout and product views sent to the Facebook pixel and to the Meta Conversions API, deduplicated with a shared event ID.
  • Customer information hashed with SHA-256 on the visitor’s device or your server (e-mail, phone in international format) to raise Event Match Quality.
  • Click IDs (fbclid) kept from the first page so the sale is tied to the ad.
  • An existing Meta pixel on the page is reused, never loaded twice.

TikTok Events API and TikTok pixel

  • The same events sent to the TikTok pixel and the TikTok Events API, with the ttclid kept for 90 days.

Google Analytics 4 and Google Ads

  • GA4 ecommerce events (view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase) with items, value and currency.
  • Google Ads conversions with enhanced conversions (hashed e-mail and phone) and the gclid kept for 90 days.

WooCommerce conversion tracking

  • Purchases sent with the order number, value, currency and items, on the classic and the block checkout.
  • An order the browser missed (blocked tag, buyer who never came back from the payment page, order entered in the admin) is sent from your server ten minutes after payment.
  • Refunds and cancellations taken back out of your reports, so your return on ad spend stays true, cash on delivery included.

Lead tracking for WordPress forms

  • Contact Form 7, Elementor Forms, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Fluent Forms, Formidable and Forminator counted as leads when their confirmation shows, not on the click.
  • HubSpot forms and Calendly bookings.
  • Phone, e-mail and WhatsApp clicks counted as contacts.

GDPR consent and Google Consent Mode v2

  • In the EEA, the UK and Switzerland the tag waits for consent before any advertising pixel loads.
  • Reads the common consent plugins (Complianz, CookieYes, Cookiebot, OneTrust, Usercentrics), Google Consent Mode v2 and any IAB TCF banner, or shows its own banner when the site has none.
  • After a refusal nothing is sent to an ad platform, from the browser or the server.

First-party mode

  • The tag and its events can go through your own domain (a REST route of this site), so a strict Content-Security-Policy or an ad blocker does not stop them.

Attribution and reports

  • Your Tagbreeze console shows which campaign and ad each sale came from, where visitors drop off on the way to the purchase, customer value by channel, and what each ad platform claims.

Who it is for

Online shops and service businesses that advertise on Facebook, Instagram, Google or TikTok without a developer, and agencies that manage several client sites.

External services

This plugin relies on the Tagbreeze service, operated by Webotic, to work.

  • What: the Tagbreeze tag is loaded from https://tagbreeze.com/t.js, or through this site in first-party mode, where this site fetches it from tagbreeze.com and keeps a copy for five minutes. The tag sends the events of each page (page viewed, product viewed, cart, checkout, purchase, form sent, contact click) to https://tagbreeze.com/e, directly or through this site.
  • When: on every front-end page, once a site key is saved in Settings > Tagbreeze. With a server key, this site also sends WooCommerce orders the browser missed, refunds and cancellations to https://tagbreeze.com/e.
  • Data sent: the event, the page address, the referring site, the order number, value, currency and items, and, with the visitor’s consent, a visitor ID, advertising click identifiers, the IP address and browser, and the e-mail and phone hashed with SHA-256. In the EEA, the UK and Switzerland, advertising data is only sent after consent.
  • Who else receives it: Tagbreeze forwards the conversions, with consent, to the ad platforms you connect in your Tagbreeze account: Meta, Google (Analytics 4 and Ads) and TikTok.
  • Tagbreeze terms of service: https://tagbreeze.com/terms/
  • Tagbreeze privacy policy: https://tagbreeze.com/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Create your site in the Tagbreeze console (14-day free trial, no card).
  2. Install and activate this plugin.
  3. Open Settings > Tagbreeze and paste the site key shown on your site’s Install screen in the console (it starts with mt_).
  4. For WooCommerce, also paste the server key from the same screen: it signs the orders, refunds and cancellations your server sends.
  5. Connect Meta, Google and TikTok in the Tagbreeze console.

Until a site key is saved, the plugin loads nothing on your site.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Tagbreeze account?

Yes. The plugin connects your site to Tagbreeze, which sends your conversions to the ad platforms and holds your reports. Plans start at 49 USD a month for one site, with a 14-day free trial.

What is server-side tracking?

Instead of relying only on a script in the visitor’s browser, each conversion is also sent from a server to the ad platform’s API (the Meta Conversions API, the TikTok Events API). Ad blockers and cookie limits cannot stop it, and a shared event ID keeps the platform from counting it twice.

Does it support the Meta Conversions API (CAPI)?

Yes. Every conversion is sent to the Facebook pixel and to the Meta Conversions API, deduplicated with the same event ID.

Do I need Google Tag Manager or a tagging server?

No. Tagbreeze runs the servers. The plugin is all you install on WordPress.

Will my sales be counted twice with my existing Facebook pixel?

No. When the same Meta pixel is already on the page, Tagbreeze does not initialise it a second time, and its browser and server events carry the same event ID.

Does it work without WooCommerce?

Yes. Without WooCommerce it tracks page views, forms, contact clicks and any conversion your tracking plan defines.

Does it support Google Consent Mode v2 and GDPR?

Yes. In the EEA, the UK and Switzerland it waits for consent, passes the visitor’s answer to Google with the four Consent Mode v2 signals, and applies it to Meta and TikTok.

Does it slow my site down?

The tag loads asynchronously and does not block the page. In first-party mode it is cached by your site for five minutes.

What about privacy?

E-mail addresses and phone numbers are hashed before anything leaves the visitor’s device or your server. In the EEA, the UK and Switzerland nothing is sent to an ad platform without consent.
sections.changelog:
1.3.2

  • A failed, pending or cancelled WooCommerce order is no longer reported as a purchase.
  • The browser and the server give an order the same event ID, so Meta and TikTok count it once.
  • Phone numbers typed without an international prefix are read with the billing country’s code (Spain, Italy, Germany…).
  • The consent answer given in the site’s own consent tool, and Global Privacy Control, now apply to the orders sent from the server.
  • Orders sent from the server carry their time, so a copied batch cannot be sent again later.
  • In first-party mode, the visitor’s country is also read from the server’s GeoIP module.

1.3.1

  • A new site key takes effect at once: the tag kept for the previous key is no longer served.

1.3.0

  • Settings page under Settings > Tagbreeze for the site key, the server key and first-party mode.
  • WooCommerce orders the browser missed, refunds and cancellations sent from the server, signed.
  • First-party mode with the visitor’s country passed on for consent.
